dedupe_keys.name: population exposure estimates in proximity to nuclear power plants country level aggregates

description: This data set gives country-level estimates of the total, urban and rural population and land area lying within set distances of nuclear power plants. It was produced by the Center for International Earth Science Information Network (CIESIN) at Columbia University to show how many people live near nuclear plants. A global point data set of plant locations was buffered at 30, 75, 150, 300, 600 and 1,200 kilometres and combined with the Global Population Count Grid Time Series Estimates for 1990, 2000 and 2010; GRUMPv1 land and unit area grids gave land area and the GRUMPv1 urban extents grid split urban from rural, all at 1 kilometre resolution. Coverage is every country with land near a plant, for the three years. The tables are downloadable from Harvard Dataverse (version 1.0, 2025) under CC-BY-4.0 at no cost. Caveats: estimates stop at 2010, plant locations reflect the source point data set, and aggregation to countries hides local detail. Simulation uses are exposure analysis for nuclear accident scenarios and emergency planning zones. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
